options: A running copy of an image
A file you use to build an image
An image that only runs on Windows
questions.explanation: An image is a template. A container is a copy of it that runs.
The format is HOST:CONTAINER. Port 8080 on your computer goes to port 80 in the container.

options: Deletes the container when it stops
Runs the container in the background
questions.explanation: -d means detached. You get your terminal back. The flag that deletes a stopped container is --rm.

questions.prompt: You change a file inside a container. Then you remove it and start a new one from the same image. Is your change still there?
options: Yes, if the image tag is the same
No, it was removed with the old container
questions.explanation: Each container has its own files, and they are removed with it. Use a volume to keep data.

questions.prompt: How do you keep database files after the container is removed?
options: Run docker commit after every change
questions.explanation: A volume lives outside the container, so it stays when the container is removed.

questions.prompt: You change only index.html and rebuild. Why is `FROM nginx:alpine` not downloaded again?
options: Docker reuses layers that did not change
It is downloaded again, just quickly
questions.explanation: Each Dockerfile step makes a layer. Docker reuses layers up to the first step that changed.

questions.prompt: In `docker build -t my-site:1.0 .`, what does the last `.` mean?
questions.explanation: The `.` is the build context: the current folder. COPY can only use files inside it.

questions.prompt: Two containers are on the same user-defined network. How can one reach the other?
options: By its container or service name
Only by a fixed IP address
questions.explanation: User-defined networks and Compose have built-in DNS. Names work as hostnames.

questions.prompt: What does `-v` add to `docker compose down`?
options: It also deletes named volumes and their data
It stops containers but keeps them
questions.explanation: down removes containers and networks. down -v also deletes volumes, and that data is gone for good.

options: It waits until the database is ready, not just started
questions.explanation: MySQL takes a few seconds to accept connections after it starts. The health check waits for that.
